items.q: First line drug treatment for severe cocaine intoxication with agitation, hypertension and hyperthermia is what?
items.exp: Benzodiazepines blunt central sympathetic outflow treating agitation, pressure, tachycardia and seizures together, with cooling and fluids. Pure beta blockade risks unopposed alpha effects dogma; antipsychotics add hyperthermia and QT burden as adjuncts only.
r: Incorrect. Unopposed alpha concern and no sedation.
Correct. Benzodiazepines calm the storm source.

items.q: Most effective single pharmacotherapy for smoking cessation on average is what?
items.exp: Varenicline partial agonism gives highest continuous abstinence among single agents, comparable to combination NRT; EAGLES trial reassured neuropsychiatric safety in stable psychiatric patients.
r: Incorrect. Single form NRT is less effective than combination.
Incorrect. Unaided quit rates are low.
Incorrect. Bupropion helps but contraindications limit universality.

items.q: Cyclical vomiting in heavy cannabis user relieved by compulsive hot showers, normal workup, is what?
items.exp: Hyperemesis syndrome follows prolonged heavy use, with hot bathing behaviour pathognomonic, resolving with sustained cessation (topical capsaicin and haloperidol are acute adjunct reports). Antiemetic cycles without cessation fail.
r: Incorrect. Withdrawal lacks this vomiting bathing pattern.
Incorrect. Diabetic gastroparesis lacks cannabis bathing clues.
Incorrect. Porphyria adds pain and neuropsychiatric pattern.
items.kp: Vomiting plus hot showers plus weed equals hyperemesis.

items.q: Methamphetamine dependence treatment with strongest evidence base is what?
items.exp: No approved agonist substitution exists; contingency management and CBT show best abstinence outcomes. Antipsychotics treat stimulant psychosis episodes only.
r: Incorrect. Sedative maintenance addicts without benefit.
items.kp: Reward abstinence, there is no stimulant methadone.

items.q: Cannabis withdrawal in heavy daily users typically peaks when and with what?
o: Days 2 to 6 with irritability, insomnia, vivid dreams and appetite loss
items.exp: Recognised withdrawal syndrome emerges 24 to 72 hours, peaks first week, mostly resolving in two weeks; it is uncomfortable not dangerous, managed supportively. Seizures suggest other substances.
r: Correct. First week irritability and insomnia peak.
Incorrect. Seizures not cannabis withdrawal feature.
items.kp: Week one grumpy and sleepless after quitting weed.

items.q: MDMA toxicity deaths commonly involve which two mechanisms?
o: Hyperthermia with serotonin toxicity and dilutional hyponatraemia from excess water
items.exp: Serotonergic hyperthermia with rhabdomyolysis and DIC plus SIADH and overhydration hyponatraemia causing cerebral oedema kill in club settings; cooling, benzodiazepines and careful fluids or hypertonic care by severity treat them.
r: Incorrect. Liver injury is late different pattern.
Incorrect. MDMA is stimulant serotonergic, not opioid.
items.kp: Hot and waterlogged: MDMA twin killers.

items.q: Ketamine chronic heavy use signature organ damage is what?
o: Ulcerative cystitis and biliary tract dilatation
items.exp: Ketamine cystitis scars and shrinks bladder with frequency, pain and haematuria, sometimes hydronephrosis; cessation early may reverse, late needs urology. Biliary dilatation and cognitive effects also reported.
r: Incorrect. Heart muscle not primary victim.

items.q: Synthetic cannabinoid (spice) intoxication differs from natural cannabis typically how?
o: More severe agitation, psychosis, seizures and deaths from full CB1 agonism
items.exp: Synthetics are potent full agonists (natural THC partial) with contaminants, producing severe neuropsychiatric and medical toxicity unpredictable by dose, managed supportively with benzodiazepines.
items.kp: Spice is cannabis chemistry without brakes.

items.q: Combination nicotine replacement means what strategy with what benefit?
o: Long acting patch plus short acting gum or lozenge for cravings, higher quit than single form
NRT indefinitely at high dose for all
items.exp: Steady patch levels plus rescue short acting doses for breakthrough cravings outperforms single form and rivals varenicline; duration typically 8 to 12 weeks with taper individualised.
r: Incorrect. Double patch is not standard combination.
Incorrect. Indefinite high dose is not default.
items.kp: Patch for baseline, gum for breakthrough.

items.q: Inhalant (volatile substance) abuse most feared acute event is what?
o: Sudden sniffing death from cardiac arrhythmia sensitised to catecholamines
items.exp: Hydrocarbons sensitise myocardium so fright or exertion adrenaline triggers fatal arrhythmia even first use; chronic use adds cognitive, renal and marrow toxicity (toluene leukoencephalopathy).
r: Incorrect. Liver not acute killer here.
Incorrect. Psychosis less defining acute risk.
Incorrect. Methanol, not typical inhalants, blinds.
items.kp: One sniff, adrenaline surge, heart stops.
